# Block reference

<!-- Generated by tools/node_docs.py from `macromagi nodes`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every block MacroMagi offers, with its ports and settings. **Flow** ports order execution (top and bottom of a block); **value** ports carry results (left and right).

The `id` under each heading is the block's type as written in `.magi` files.

## Flow

Where a macro starts, waits, loops, branches and stops.

### Decision

`flow.decision`

Chooses which branch to follow. Each case has a condition input on the left; the first case whose condition is true wins. If none is true, “Else” is followed.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: **one per case**, **Else**
- Value inputs: **one condition per case** (true/false)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cases | list of cases | one case |  |

### Wait

`flow.delay`

Pauses for a set time before continuing.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Duration | duration | 500 ms |  |
| Random ± | duration | 0 ms | Vary each wait by a random amount up to this, so the timing looks less mechanical. |

### Log

`flow.log`

Writes a line to the console. Handy for checking which path a macro took.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Value** (any value)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Message | text | Reached this step |  |

### Repeat

`flow.repeat`

Runs the blocks under “Loop” over and over, then continues from “Done”. When the looped branch reaches its end it automatically returns here.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: **Loop**, **Done**

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Repeat | choice | A number of times | Options: A number of times; Until stopped. |
| Times | whole number | 10 × |  |

### Start

`flow.start`

Where a macro begins. A macro can have several Start blocks; each one runs independently and can have its own hotkey.

- Flow out: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hotkey | hotkey | none | Any keyboard key, mouse button or gamepad button, alone or combined. |
| Hotkey behaviour | choice | Toggle | Options: Toggle – press to start, press again to stop; Hold – run while the hotkey is held; Press – start on every press. |
| Start with the Run button | on/off | on | Turn off for blocks that should only ever be started by their hotkey. |

### Stop

`flow.stop`

Ends the macro here.

- Flow in: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stop | choice | This Start block only | Options: This Start block only; The whole macro. |

### Wait Until

`flow.wait_until`

Pauses until its condition becomes true, checking at a regular interval.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: **Then**, **Timed out**
- Value inputs: **Condition** (true/false)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Check every | duration | 100 ms |  |
| Give up after | duration | 0 ms | Zero means wait for as long as it takes. |

## Input

Sending keyboard and mouse input.

### Input

`input.action`

Sends input: a key, a mouse click, a move, a scroll or typed text. Add several inputs to one block to perform them at the same time, like Ctrl + C.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Position** (screen position)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Inputs | list of inputs | one left click |  |
| Hold time | duration | 30 ms | How long taps and clicks stay pressed before they are released. |

### Auto Click

`input.autoclick`

Clicks (or presses keys) over and over at a steady speed, with everything the Auto Clicker tab offers: speed variation, duty cycle, limits, corner and edge stops.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clicking | Auto Clicker settings | left click, 10 per second, until stopped |  |

### Play Recording

`input.recording`

Replays recorded input with its original timing: every key and button is pressed and released exactly when it was during recording.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recording | recording | none |  |
| Speed | number | 1 × |  |
| Replay mouse movement | on/off | on |  |
| Mouse movement as | choice | As recorded (smart) | Games with a first-person camera lock the pointer and read how far the mouse moves. If the camera turns once and then stops, choose relative motion. Options: As recorded (smart); Screen positions; Relative motion – for games. |

## Vision

Looking at the screen. These are value blocks: they have no place in the order of execution and are evaluated whenever another block reads them.

### Color Detection

`vision.find_color`

Looks for a colour on screen. “Found” is true when at least one pixel in the search area matches; “Position” is the first matching pixel.

- Value outputs: **Found** (true/false), **Position** (screen position)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Color | colour | #FF3B30 |  |
| Tolerance | whole number | 16 | How far red, green and blue may each be off and still count as a match. |
| Search area | screen area | whole screen |  |

### Image Detection

`vision.find_image`

Looks for an image on screen. “Found” is true when a match at least as similar as the accuracy setting exists; “Position” is the centre of the best match. Wire “Found” into a Decision or Wait Until, and “Position” into an Input to click it.

- Value outputs: **Found** (true/false), **Position** (screen position), **Similarity** (number)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Image | image | none |  |
| Search area | screen area | whole screen | A smaller area is faster and avoids false matches elsewhere on screen. |
| Accuracy | percentage | 80% | How closely the screen must match the image. 100% demands a pixel-perfect match. |

## Window

Working with program windows.

### Switch to Window

`window.focus`

Brings a program's window to the front (restoring it if it is minimised) and waits until it is ready for input. Knows how windowed, borderless and exclusive fullscreen programs behave, or works it out itself.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: **Switched**, **Not found**
- Value outputs: **Screen type** (text)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Window | text |  | Part of the window's title, or of the program's name, e.g. “Minecraft” or “game.exe”. |
| Find it by | choice | Window title | Options: Window title; Program name. |
| Screen type | choice | Detect automatically | Exclusive fullscreen programs need longer to come back after a switch. Options: Detect automatically; Windowed; Borderless fullscreen; Exclusive fullscreen. |
| Keep looking for | duration | 2000 ms |  |

## Logic

Combining and producing true/false values.

### Random Chance

`logic.chance`

True some of the time, at random. Use it to make a macro less predictable.

- Value outputs: **Result** (true/false)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chance of true | percentage | 50% |  |

### Logic

`logic.gate`

Combines true/false values: AND, OR, XOR, or NOT (which only uses input A).

- Value inputs: **A** (true/false), **B** (true/false)
- Value outputs: **Result** (true/false)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Operation | choice | A and B | Options: A and B; A or B; Exactly one of A, B; Not A. |

## Script

Your own code as a step of the macro.

### Python Script

`script.python` · Python engine only

Runs your own Python code as a step of the macro. The script can send input, read the screen and compute a result for other blocks. Needs the Python engine.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Value** (any value)
- Value outputs: **Result** (any value)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Code | code | a commented starter script |  |
